traits.observation: Numerous long, fine, leafy branchlets hang steeply downward, forming conspicuous curtains around the crown and extending toward the ground.
Exposed lower trunks are pale white to silvery gray with irregular dark marks and patches. Fine bark texture is unresolved.
Foliage reads as many small, discrete leaf flecks along slender hanging shoots, producing a fine, stippled texture rather than broad, solid foliage masses.
The crown has an irregular, broadly spreading outline with elevated tufts, outward arching shoulders, and long cascading margins. Its uppermost extent is cropped.
At least two conspicuous slender pale stems rise close together near the base; one is comparatively upright and another leans outward. Their exact basal connection is obscured.
Overlapping foliage curtains alternate with narrow openings and deep shaded recesses. The perimeter is finely broken, while portions of the interior appear dense.
Some visible pale branches extend outward in arches before finer growth descends. Most internal branch junctions are hidden by foliage.

Visible foliage ranges from pale yellow-green or silvery green flecks to medium green and very dark green recesses. Intrinsic leaf color cannot be separated confidently from illumination and photographic rendering.
Within this crown, hanging shoots differ substantially in length, spacing, and density; some form compact drapes, while others appear as isolated strands.
Foliage masses and gaps are distributed asymmetrically, with differing heights and widths across the crown. The exact silhouette is evidence from this view only.

observations: Only reference-0 is supplied; no relationship between specimens or change over time can be assessed.
The strongest visible recognition cues are pendulous fine shoots, small-scale foliage texture, and pale trunks with dark markings.
Individual leaf shape, serration, venation, buds, flowers, and fruit are not reliably resolved.
Background vegetation overlaps the right crown boundary, limiting certainty about its full spread.
The image shows a pronounced weeping habit, but its cause and representativeness across the target species remain undetermined.
Variation entries describe visible differences within this reference; broader acceptable species variation is not established by this single view.
